high.title: Vietnam Stock Market Awaits Major September Event: ~$128M in Vietnamese Equities Could Enter FTSE Radar
high.summary:
Vietnam's market upgrade to **FTSE Emerging Market (EM) status** is now confirmed for **September 2026**, marking one of the most significant structural capital flow events for Vietnamese equities in years. FTSE Russell will officially announce the eligible stock list on **August 21, 2026**, with index inclusion effective **September 21, 2026**.

ACBS Securities estimates **19 Vietnamese stocks** will meet FTSE GEIS selection criteria based on data through June 30, 2026 — comprising 4 large-cap, 1 mid-cap, and 14 small-cap names. **Estimated net passive inflows for the September rebalancing period are approximately $128 million USD (~VND 3,371 billion).**

high.title: VN-Index Falls 150 Points From Peak — Is the Bottom Now in Sight?
high.summary: The VN-Index has retreated to its lowest level in nearly three months, having broken below the psychologically critical 1,800-point threshold. The index has shed approximately 100 points since the start of July and is down roughly 150 points from its recent peak. According to Mr. Luong Duy Phuoc, Head of Market Research at Kafi Securities, the correction reflects a confluence of external and domestic headwinds. On the external front, escalating US-Iran geopolitical tensions have driven Brent crude prices sharply higher — from ~$72/bbl to above $82/bbl in a short window — reigniting global inflation concerns and raising expectations that the Fed will maintain an elevated interest rate posture longer than markets had priced. This "higher-for-longer" dynamic is directly pressuring risk appetite and capital flows toward emerging markets including Vietnam. Domestically, foreign investors have continued net selling, while liquidity conditions have deteriorated and retail investor sentiment has turned cautious. **Key watch:** whether foreign net selling stabilizes, and whether the index finds technical support at current levels or risks further downside. For VND and bond investors, sustained equity outflows amplify FX pressure and could complicate SBV's liquidity management.

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of July 15 — ACB Leads at 7.3% p.a. for 12-Month Tenor
high.summary: Vietnam's retail deposit rate landscape remains elevated, with ACB offering the highest rate in the 12-month tenor at 7.3% per annum, followed closely by Saigonbank (7.2%), Bac A Bank (7.1%), and a cluster of three banks — MBV, VCBNeo, and VIB — at 7.0%. Notably, six banks are now offering 12-month deposit rates at or above 7.0% p.a., signaling persistent competition for retail funding. The next tier — LPBank, BVBank, OCB, and PGBank — sits at 6.9% for the 12-month tenor, with LPBank leading at 6.95% for 18-month deposits. **Market implications:** The persistence of deposit rates in the 6.9%–7.3% range at smaller and mid-tier banks suggests liquidity demand remains firm across the system despite SBV's accommodative posture. Elevated deposit rates act as a floor for lending rates and government bond yields, making aggressive duration extension in VGB positions less compelling. Fund managers should monitor whether the major state-owned banks (Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) begin repricing upward — which would signal broader systemic tightening pressure.

medium.title: VN-Index Struggles Near 1,800 Points: Nearly 900 Stocks in Negative Territory, Investor Portfolios Down Double Digits
medium.summary: The VN-Index continues to trade sideways near the 1,800-point level, roughly flat versus the start of 2026. However, the headline index masks significant underlying weakness: out of more than 1,500 listed stocks across all three exchanges, 888 stocks are in negative territory year-to-date, with over 200 having declined more than 20%. Notable names including FPT, SSI, VRE, DXG, and SHS are among the losers. Individual investors report portfolio drawdowns of 15–30%+, particularly in mid-cap names. The divergence between the flat index and broad market deterioration suggests heavy rotation into a narrow set of large-cap index constituents, masking genuine market stress. For fund managers, this breadth deterioration is a cautionary signal — elevated retail losses could dampen domestic liquidity and risk appetite on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange in the near term. Watch for any SBV commentary on market stability or liquidity support measures.

medium.title: Gold Bar and Ring Prices Continue Sharp Decline on July 14 — Buyers Immediately Down Nearly VND 5 Million/Tael
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices fell sharply on July 14, with SJC gold bars dropping VND 1.3 million/tael on both the bid and ask sides to VND 144.1–147.1 million/tael. Ring gold (vàng nhẫn) saw similar declines of VND 0.8–1.3 million/tael across major dealers including Bảo Tín Minh Châu, Bảo Tín Mạnh Hải, and DOJI. The bid-ask spread implies an immediate mark-to-market loss of nearly VND 5 million/tael for retail buyers. While gold price movements are primarily driven by international spot prices, sustained domestic gold price declines are worth monitoring as they can influence household asset allocation behavior, reduce demand for FX to fund gold imports, and modestly ease pressure on the VND/USD rate.

medium.title: Over VND 9.4 Quadrillion in Customer Deposits Flowed Into 27 Banks Over the Past Decade: Which Bank Attracted the Most Deposits?
medium.summary:
Total customer deposits across 27 listed Vietnamese banks surged from approximately VND 3.4 quadrillion at end-2015 to over VND 12.8 quadrillion by end-2025 — a near 4x increase over the decade, with an average annual inflow of roughly VND 940 trillion. The article attributes this growth to a broadening economy, rising household incomes, expanding corporate balance sheets, and accelerating digital banking adoption. For bond and FX investors, this data point is meaningful: the sustained accumulation of deposit liabilities signals robust domestic liquidity within the banking system, which underpins the SBV's ability to manage monetary conditions. A deep and growing deposit base also supports system-wide credit expansion and reduces banks' reliance on wholesale or external funding — a credit-positive factor. However, investors should monitor whether deposit growth is keeping pace with loan growth, as widening gaps could pressure net interest margins or signal loosening of lending standards. The trend also reinforces VND stability narratives, as strong domestic savings reduce dollarization risk.

---

medium.title: $10 Billion Pharmaceutical Sector Attracts Foreign Capital: M&A Race for Vietnamese Pharma Companies Heats Up
medium.summary: Vietnam's pharmaceutical sector, projected to reach $10 billion in market value, is attracting accelerating foreign capital inflows through M&A activity. Both international pharmaceutical conglomerates and domestic financial groups are competing for stakes in Vietnamese pharma companies with established production capacity and distribution networks. According to SHS Research, the 2025–2030 period is expected to mark a new growth cycle as the industry transitions from generic drug manufacturing toward modern production ecosystems compliant with international standards. While not a direct FX or bond market driver, sustained foreign M&A inflows into the sector represent a meaningful source of USD inflows that can provide modest support to the VND. Fund managers with equity mandates should monitor listed pharma names for re-rating potential driven by foreign strategic acquisitions.

medium.title: A Turbulent Week for Gold and Silver Prices
medium.summary:
Gold and silver markets experienced broad-based declines during the trading week of July 6–12, 2026, pressured by a recovering US Dollar, hawkish Fed signaling, and renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Domestic SJC gold bars closed the week at VND 146.9 million/tael (bid) and VND 149.9 million/tael (ask), with prices extending losses into the following Monday (July 13), trading in the VND 145–148.4 million/tael range — down approximately 1.6% over seven days. For VND traders, USD strength is the key transmission mechanism here: a firmer dollar tends to exert depreciation pressure on the VND and may complicate SBV's FX management efforts. Watch whether continued USD strength forces SBV intervention in the FX market or prompts adjustments to the central rate in the sessions ahead.

---

medium.title: VinaCapital Expert Speaks Candidly on Stock Market Paradox
medium.summary:
VinaCapital's Senior Investment Director, Mr. Dinh Duc Minh, highlights a growing paradox in Vietnam's equity market: the VN-Index headline performance is being driven almost entirely by Vingroup-related stocks, while the **broader market is effectively down ~5% year-to-date** when Vingroup stocks are excluded. Average daily liquidity has fallen sharply to ~**$500M/session**, roughly half the levels seen at the start of the year — a sign of weakening market breadth and investor participation. Paradoxically, corporate fundamentals remain solid: **HoSE-listed company profits grew ~37% in Q1 2026**, with VinaCapital forecasting a further **15-20% profit growth in Q2**. This divergence between falling prices and rising earnings has pushed valuations to increasingly attractive levels. For international fund managers, this signals a potential **mean-reversion opportunity in Vietnamese equities**, though thin liquidity remains a key execution risk. The macro headwinds weighing on sentiment — likely including USD strength and global risk-off dynamics — bear close monitoring.

---

medium.title: Bank Earnings Update July 15: More Banks Report Surging Profits
medium.summary:
Vietbank reported preliminary H1 2026 pre-tax profit of VND 923 billion, up 79.4% year-on-year, driven primarily by a 26% surge in net interest income to VND 1,747 billion. Total assets crossed VND 205,000 billion (+4% YTD), loan balances grew 11% to VND 120,294 billion, and customer deposits rose 5.6% to VND 132,369 billion. For full-year 2026, Vietbank targets 23.6% credit growth and pre-tax profit of VND 2,100 billion. BVBank also reported positive preliminary figures with total assets estimated up ~7% versus end-2025. The strong banking sector earnings broadly reflect healthy credit demand and an improving net interest margin environment. For fixed income investors, robust bank profitability reduces tail risk in the financial sector but also reinforces expectations of sustained credit growth — a variable the SBV will weigh carefully when calibrating future monetary policy moves.

---

medium.title: VinaCapital Expert Speaks Candidly About a Paradox in the Stock Market
medium.summary: VinaCapital's Senior Investment Director, Mr. Dinh Duc Minh, highlighted a notable disconnect in Vietnam's equity market: excluding Vingroup-related stocks, the broader market is effectively down ~5% year-to-date, while average daily liquidity has fallen to ~USD 500 million per session — roughly half of early-year levels. This contrasts sharply with strong corporate fundamentals: HoSE-listed earnings grew ~37% in Q1 2026, with VinaCapital projecting continued 15–20% growth in Q2. The expert attributes the divergence to multiple simultaneous macroeconomic headwinds weighing on investor sentiment. For fund managers, this valuation dislocation — improving earnings versus declining prices — may signal a medium-term re-rating opportunity, particularly ahead of the FTSE EM upgrade in September which could serve as a sentiment catalyst.

medium.title: Ministry of Industry and Trade: No Exploitation of Market Volatility for Price Gouging or Hoarding
medium.summary: Vietnam's Ministry of Industry and Trade (MoIT) has issued a firm public stance against any exploitation of current market volatility — including rising oil prices and supply disruptions — to unjustifiably raise prices, hoard goods, or profiteer. The ministry confirmed it retains regulatory authority over key price-sensitive commodities including petroleum, electricity, LPG, and construction steel, and is actively monitoring domestic and global supply-demand and pricing dynamics. This statement is notable in the context of Brent crude rising sharply above $82/barrel, which creates upward pressure on fuel and energy prices in Vietnam. For macro watchers, this signals the government's intent to contain administered price increases — a factor that could help moderate headline CPI in the near term, providing the SBV with slightly more room to maintain accommodative monetary policy. However, if global energy prices remain elevated, suppressing domestic prices may prove difficult to sustain and could resurface as an inflation risk later in Q3 2026.

medium.title: Vietnam Surpasses US as China Becomes Top Seafood Export Destination
medium.summary: Vietnam's seafood exports reached over $5.7 billion in H1 2026, up 11.4% year-on-year, with China overtaking the US as the largest single market — importing nearly $1.4 billion worth (+40% YoY) versus the US at ~$898 million. Including Hong Kong, the greater China region absorbed ~$1.5 billion (+38%). Japan ranked third at ~$788 million. The strong export diversification toward China reduces Vietnam's vulnerability to US trade policy risks and supports the trade balance. For FX traders, sustained export growth — particularly with China — is a positive structural USD inflow driver for VND, helping underpin the currency against broader EM headwinds. This data point is relevant to the current account outlook for H2 2026.
